answer_text: Bakingg soda is sodiumm hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO3. On heating it gives carbon dioxide, wich makes cakes rise; it is also a mild antacid and is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers. Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO4.1/2H2O. It is obtained by heating gypsum, CaSO4.2H2O, at about 373 K so that it loses water. Mixed with water it sets to a hard mass and is used to support fractured bones.
